newsitem.title: UK: UK prompt natgas softer on system sell, quiet late.
newsitem.headline: UK prompt natgas softer on system sell, quiet late.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market was weaker on Wednesday, traders and brokers said. But the market was unusually quiet with many players away from London on a trip organised by a market participant.
The short term market was actively traded, with significant trade seen on the within day, day ahead and balance of the month markets.

Within day prices fell as there were two system sells on the flexibility mechanism, one in the morning and one in the afternoon. A trader said that the System Average Price (SAP) for the sales was around 9.28 pence a therm, and this pushed prices down on both the within day and day ahead markets.
Further out, levels were off on average by around 0.10 pence a therm, dealers said. "It's off on the basis that there are few people around and it's difficult to assess," a trader said.

The fourth quarter was traded at 13 pence a therm, and rumoured done on an unconfirmed basis at 12.925 pence a therm. There were also widespread rumours that a Q4/Q1 strip had traded at 14.70 pence a therm, with one broker saying that Q4 was valued at 12.95 pence and Q1 at 16.45 pence.
Rumours were also heard of an identical strip done at 14.65 pence a therm, but these were both unconfirmed.

If the spot market was quiet, the futures market was even more so. No trade was done at all on Wednesday, and by the close only a single bid was posted, for August at 9.90 pence a therm, with only a single offer, in July at 9.85 pence a therm.
